dimensions.assessment: Affects oil and gas operators on nonfederal surface estates with partially federal mineral rights, the Bureau of Land Management, and state permitting agencies.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall not require an operator to obtain a Federal drilling permit for oil and gas exploration and production activities conducted on non-Federal surface estate

dimensions.assessment: Eliminates federal permitting requirements and major environmental reviews for qualifying oil and gas activities, allowing operations to commence 30 days after state permit submission.
dimensions.evidence: shall not be considered a major Federal action for the purposes of section 102(2)(C) of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969

dimensions.assessment: Does not affect federal royalties or auditing authority under the Federal Oil and Gas Royalty Management Act of 1982.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this subsection shall affect the amount of royalties due to the United States under this Act from the production of oil and gas

dimensions.assessment: Amends Section 17 of the Mineral Leasing Act to carve out explicit exemptions from NEPA, NHPA, and the Endangered Species Act for specific drilling units.
dimensions.evidence: Section 17 of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 226) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory exemption from federal permitting and environmental reviews for eligible oil and gas activities.

missing_information: The total acreage or number of drilling units nationwide that meet the criteria of having less than 50 percent federal mineral ownership on nonfederal surface estates.
Expected changes in federal administrative workload or inspection frequency.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill exempts certain oil and gas exploration and production on nonfederal surface estates with partial federal mineral rights from federal drilling permits and major environmental reviews under NEPA, NHPA, and ESA.
